title: Sensitive Data, Secrets, Ephemeral Values and Write-Only Arguments

header.html: 4h Understand best practices for managing sensitive data, including secrets management with Vault, ephemeral values and write-only arguments
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1Sensitive values

Marking a variable or output sensitive = true hides it in CLI output (shown as (sensitive value)).

variable "db_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

output "connection_string" {
  value     = "postgres://admin:${var.db_password}@db.example.com/app"
  sensitive = true
}
Fact Detail
What it hides The value in plan and apply output and in terraform output
What it does not hide The value is still stored in the state file and in saved plan files, in plain text
Derived values A value built from a sensitive value must also be marked sensitive
Reading it anyway terraform output -json or the state can show it to someone with access
Exam tip

. sensitive hides, it does not encrypt. Protect the state and plan files as secrets.

2Best practices for secrets

Practice Why
Never hard-code secrets in .tf files They end up in version control
Do not commit terraform.tfvars with secrets Same reason
Supply secrets from the environment: TF_VAR_name or provider variables such as AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Not written to files
Use a secrets manager such as HashiCorp Vault Central, audited, rotated secrets
Prefer short-lived and dynamic credentials A leaked value expires quickly
Encrypt and restrict the state The state may contain secrets

3HashiCorp Vault with Terraform

Vault is a secrets management product. Terraform can read secrets from Vault with the Vault provider and a data source.

provider "vault" {
  address = "https://vault.example.com:8200"
}

data "vault_kv_secret_v2" "db" {
  mount = "secret"
  name  = "app/database"
}

resource "aws_db_instance" "main" {
  identifier        = "example"
  engine            = "mysql"
  instance_class    = "db.t3.micro"
  allocated_storage = 20
  username          = data.vault_kv_secret_v2.db.data["username"]
  password          = data.vault_kv_secret_v2.db.data["password"]
}
Fact Detail
Authentication A token or other method, supplied through VAULT_TOKEN or provider settings, not hard-coded
The catch A secret read through a data source is stored in the state
Better Dynamic secrets from Vault (short-lived credentials), and ephemeral values (next sections)
Exam tip

. Reading a secret from Vault into an ordinary attribute still puts it in the state. Ephemeral values and write-only arguments were added to avoid that.

4Ephemeral values (new in 004)

An ephemeral value exists only during the run and is never saved in the plan or the state.

Kind Example
Ephemeral input variable ephemeral = true in a variable block
Ephemeral resource An ephemeral block that opens a temporary resource such as a generated password or a secret fetched at run time
Ephemeral output In a child module, ephemeral = true in an output block 
variable "api_token" {
  type      = string
  ephemeral = true
}

ephemeral "random_password" "db" {
  length = 20
}

Where an ephemeral value may be used: provider configuration, write-only arguments, other ephemeral contexts. Terraform refuses to use one in an ordinary resource argument, because that would save it in state.

5Write-only arguments (new in 004)

A write-only argument is a resource argument that accepts a value, uses it and never stores it in the plan or state. By convention its name ends in _wo, and a companion _wo_version argument tells Terraform when to send a new value.

resource "aws_db_instance" "main" {
  identifier          = "example"
  engine              = "mysql"
  instance_class      = "db.t3.micro"
  allocated_storage   = 20
  username            = "admin"
  password_wo         = ephemeral.random_password.db.result
  password_wo_version = 1
}
Fact Detail
Stored in state? No; the value is never saved
How to change it Change the _wo_version number, so Terraform sends the new value again
Combine with Ephemeral values, so the secret never touches the state
Exam tip

. Ephemeral = not saved. Write-only argument = accepts an ephemeral value and does not store it. _wo_version is how you trigger an update.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A variable is marked sensitive. Where can its value still be found?

  • AIn the plan output on the screen
  • BIn the output of terraform fmt
  • CIn the state file, in plain text
  • DIn the lock file of the providers
Show the answer

Answer: C. Sensitive values are hidden in CLI output but remain in state and in saved plans.

S2What is the best way to supply a database password to a configuration that is stored in version control?

  • AWrite it in the variable default
  • BCommit it in terraform.tfvars
  • CPass it through an environment variable or a secrets manager
  • DPut it in a comment next to the variable
Show the answer

Answer: C. Secrets should come from the environment or a secrets manager, not from files in version control.

S3A configuration reads a secret from Vault through a data source and uses it in an ordinary argument. What is true?

  • AThe secret is not stored anywhere
  • BThe secret is stored in the state
  • CThe secret is stored in the provider lock file
  • DThe secret is deleted after the plan
Show the answer

Answer: B. Values read through a data source and used in ordinary arguments are saved in state.

S4Which value is never saved in the plan or the state?

  • AA sensitive variable
  • BAn ephemeral value
  • CA local value
  • DAn output value
Show the answer

Answer: B. Ephemeral values exist only during the run and are not persisted.

S5What is a write-only argument?

  • AAn argument that accepts a value without storing it in the plan or state
  • BAn argument that can only be read after apply
  • CAn argument that is written to the lock file
  • DAn argument that must be set in the backend block
Show the answer

Answer: A. A write-only argument uses the value but never saves it.

S6How can a team make Terraform send a new value for a write-only password argument?

  • AChange the matching _wo_version value
  • BRun terraform fmt on the file and apply it
  • CDelete the state file
  • DMark the variable as sensitive
Show the answer

Answer: A. The companion version argument signals Terraform to send the new value again.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Does sensitive encrypt a value in the state?

Show the answer

No, it only hides it in CLI output.

R2Name one good way to supply a secret.

Show the answer

An environment variable or a secrets manager.

R3Which provider reads secrets from Vault?

Show the answer

The Vault provider.

R4Where are ephemeral values stored?

Show the answer

Nowhere; they are not saved in plan or state.

R5What does a write-only argument name usually end in?

Show the answer

_wo.

R6What does _wo_version do?

Show the answer

Triggers sending a new write-only value.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
sensitive hides in CLI output; still in state and plans
Secrets never hard-code; environment or secrets manager; short-lived credentials
Vault Vault provider and data sources; data source values land in state
Ephemeral not saved: variables, resources, child module outputs
Write-only _wo arguments take ephemeral values and are not stored; _wo_version triggers updates
